header.name: Enhancement Technologies and the Body: Beyond the Human Form
header.description: This course examines how technological, biomedical and bioengineering interventions in human form make it possible to alter the biological form and function of the human body from an anthropological perspective. It traces how cultural assumptions about the “normal” and “deficient” bodies come to be constructed and how body-altering medical technologies are used to “enhance” human form, which not only repair or replace functions, but may go beyond what is typically considered therapeutic medical intervention. Drawing on anthropological perspectives grounded in feminist theory, socio-materialism, cyborg theory, critical disability studies and trans and post-humanist critiques of the human this course will examine the social, political and ethical consequences of technological bodily innovations and enhancements. Mapping a range of medical interventions—NRTs, Hormones, Prosthetics, Digital Technologies to Wearable Augmentations—this course will equip learners in analyzing the impact these interventions have on understanding of the body, social identity, embodiment, social relations and social institutions.
prerequisites_mandatory: Introduction to Sociology and Anthropology (SOC 101) or equivalent
prerequisites_desirable: Science, Technology and Society (SOC 211) OR Sociological Theory (SOC210) OR Advanced Sociological Theory (SOC312/SOC502)
prerequisites_mandatory_resolved: Introduction to Sociology and Anthropology (SOC 101) or equivalent
prerequisites_desirable_resolved: Science, Technology and Society (SOC 211) OR Sociological Theory (SOC210) OR Advanced Sociological Theory (SOC312/SOC502)

outcomes.label: CO1
outcomes.raw_text: Learners will identify how the ideas of natural or normal body came to be defined around mid-nineteenth century and how these shifted over time.

outcomes.label: CO2
outcomes.raw_text: They will understand and interpret social construction of the biological body and analyze technological enhancements as body projects.

outcomes.label: CO3
outcomes.raw_text: They will be able to critically evaluate claims about technological enhancement of the body

outcomes.label: CO4
outcomes.raw_text: They will be able to critique implications of biomedical and technological interventions into the human form from socio-political, cultural and ethical dimensions across a range of social contexts and diverse technological interventions

outcomes.label: CO5
outcomes.raw_text: They will be able to apply critical theories to develop original arguments about the implications of biomedical interventions into the human form.

lecture_topics: Introduction- The ‘Natural’/ ‘Normal’ Body? Or The Socially Constructed Body?
Bariatric Surgery and the Metabolic body
Prosthetic Technologies: From Cotton to Silicone Bodies
Plastic Surgery and the Gendered Body
Bionic Technologies and the Replaceable Body
Digital Technologies and the Quantified Body
Wearable Augmentations and the Informed Body

assessments.type_label: Final Term Paper (instead of End-sem exam)
